title: SoK: Reconstruction Attacks on Synthetic Tabular Data (Insights from Winning the NIST CRC) — research artifact
description:
The complete experiment framework behind the PoPETs 2027 paper SoK: Reconstruction Attacks on Synthetic Tabular Data (Insights from Winning the NIST CRC).

It contains implementations of every reconstruction attack in the paper's taxonomy, including the six the paper introduces (CoBP-RA, CondMST, CondDDPM, CondRePaint, ARFFormer, MultiHeadMLP); the composable chaining and ensembling wrappers; the synthetic-data-generation layer covering all nine evaluated generators plus four further differentially private mechanisms used for the epsilon sweep; and the rarity-weighted reconstruction-advantage scoring code that was also the official NIST Collaborative Research Cycle metric.

It also ships results.db, a SQLite database of all 49,126 scored attack runs behind the paper, together with reproduce.py, which regenerates the paper's tables and figures from it. DATABASE.md documents that database for use as a standalone dataset, independently of this framework.

Evaluation is four CPU-only commands in a provided Docker image; ./test.sh verifies the environment end to end in about two minutes. No GPU is required.

Note on this archive: automatically generated source archives do not include git submodule contents. The external/recon-synth and external/MIA_on_diffusion directories will be empty here. Everything needed for the paper's tables, the test suite and the reduced-scale experiments works without them; only the diffusion attacks and LinearReconstruction require them. To obtain those, clone with git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/steveng9/Reconstruction.git.
